Terms and Conditions
FOREWORD AND INTERPRETATION
This document sets out the general terms and conditions for the use of Data as provided by the London Stock Exchange plc (“LSE”) and/or Turquoise
Global Holdings Limited (“TGHL”).
This document provides a unified set of terms for Customers of all or either of the Exchange’s Data Products, and together with the Schedules, and
the applicable Order Form, form the Agreement and independent legal relationship between each of the Exchanges and the Customer.
If an Order Form is executed by:
(a) the Customer and LSE only, the parties to the Agreement shall be the Customer and LSE;
(b) the Customer and TGHL only, the parties to the Agreement shall be the Customer and TGHL;
(c) the Customer, LSE and TGHL, the effect of the Agreement will be to create independent legal relationships on identical terms: (i) one
between the Customer and LSE; and (ii) one between the Customer and TGHL.
The Data Shop Agreement shall be an independent and separate agreement for Data Shop Products between the Customer and the relevant
Exchange. All other Data Products shall be subject to the Agreement.
Please also refer to the relevant policies and price lists applicable to your subscription set out in the Schedules for further rules and guidance.

. Each Exchange (where relevant) shall take all reasonable steps to provide the Service to the Customer on the terms and conditions contained
in the Agreement.
. Notwithstanding anything else in the Agreement, the parties acknowledge and agree that:

. LSE is solely responsible for providing the Service (and any related obligations) to the Customer to the extent the Service or related
obligation relates to LSE Data; and

. TGHL is solely responsible for providing the Service (and any related obligations) to the Customer to the extent the Service or related
obligation relates to TGHL or TGHE Data.

. Subject to the Customer’s compliance with the terms of the Agreement, each Exchange hereby grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-
transferable, revocable, worldwide licence during the Initial Term and each Renewal Term (as applicable) to:
. use the Data for limited internal use;

. back up and store the Data in so far as it is necessary for:
2.1.3.1. compliance with the Reporting and Audit Schedule;
2.1.3.2. reasonable internal financial record keeping; and
2.1.3.3. compliance with the laws and regulations applicable to the Customer,
together, the “Limited Licence”.

. Subject to any further licence granted in accordance with clause 2.3, each Exchange hereby expressly reserves all rights (including Intellectual
Property Rights), licences and permissions in and to the Data and the Trade Marks, other than the limited rights granted under clause 2.1.

. In the event that the Customer wishes to licence the Data for the Licensable Activities in addition to the Limited Licence, from the
Commencement Date as stated on an executed Order Form, each Exchange hereby grants the Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable,
revocable, worldwide licence during the Initial Term and each Renewal Term (as applicable) to use the Data for the Licensable Activities
specified on the Order Form subject to:
. compliance with the further terms relevant to each Licensable Activity as set out in the Market Data Policy Schedule (as applicable);
. in respect of the Customer’s own use of the Data, the terms of the Limited Licence;

. in the event that the Customer provides access to the Data to any third party (for example as a result of the Customer having a Redistribution
Licence) the Customer shall procure that the third party complies with the terms of the Limited Licence; and
. the Customer attributing the source of the Data to the Exchange, using the relevant Trade Mark.

sections.title: SUBSIDIARIES
sections.text: London Stock Exchange Market Data Terms and Conditions
. The Customer’s Subsidiaries specifically listed on an executed Order Form may use the relevant Data, provided that:

. the Customer shall procure that the Subsidiaries comply with the Customer’s relevant obligations under the Agreement (other than payment
of the Charges) and shall be liable for any breach by a Subsidiary;

. the Subsidiaries shall not be third party beneficiaries under the Agreement and the Customer shall procure that no Subsidiaries bring a Claim
against either Exchange in relation to the Agreement, provided that any Losses incurred by a Subsidiary in relation to the Data shall be
recoverable by the Customer to the extent such Losses would be recoverable if incurred by the Customer; and
. unless otherwise stated, notices served upon the Customer shall be deemed to be served at the same time upon the Subsidiaries.

. The Customer shall provide the Exchanges with any applicable reporting in accordance with the Market Data Policy Schedule and the Reporting
and Audit Schedule (except for Customers solely subject to the Data Shop Agreement).

. The Customer shall allow each Exchange and their agents access to operational controls, systems, records and other documents relating to
the Service, permit each Exchange to take copies or extracts, and supply copies on demand to the relevant Exchange to verify compliance with
the Agreement in accordance with the Reporting and Audit Schedule.

. The Agreement will become effective on the Commencement Date and shall remain in force until the end of the Initial Term. Upon expiry of the
Initial Term, the Agreement will continue for each Renewal Term, unless and until terminated in accordance with the terms of the Agreement.

. Either party may terminate the Agreement effective on the expiration of the Initial Term, or twelve (12) months following the Commencement
Date, whichever is later, with at least ninety (90) calendar days’ written notice. Following the expiration of the Initial Term or the first twelve (12)
months of the Commencement Date, whichever is later, either party may terminate the Agreement with at least ninety (90) calendar days’ written
notice.

. Either party may terminate a specific use within the list of Licensable Activities on an Order Form, with at least ninety (90) calendar days’ written
notice to the other party, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the relevant Exchange. All other uses and the licences held for such uses within
the Licensable Activities listed on the Order Form shall remain unaffected by such termination and shall continue in full force and effect for the
remainder of the Initial Term and any subsequent Renewal Term unless terminated earlier in accordance with the terms of the Agreement. .
. Any notice given in accordance with 5.2 above will be effective from the last calendar day of the month in which the notice is given.
. Either party may terminate the Agreement immediately by giving the other party written notice if that other party:

. becomes unable to pay its debts in the ordinary course of business, passes a resolution for winding up or has a receiver or administrator
appointed over all or any of its assets, becomes insolvent (whether voluntarily or involuntarily), is placed in liquidation, or ceases to carry on
business as a going concern or the equivalent occurs in any jurisdiction; or

. materially breaches any of its obligations under the Agreement (including but not limited to, in the case of Customer, payment of Charges to
the Exchanges and use of the Data in accordance with the Limited Licence at clause 2) and does not remedy such failure, if capable of remedy,
within 30 (thirty) days of receiving notice from the Exchange requiring it to do so.
. Either Exchange may terminate the Agreement or suspend all or part of the Service without liability if:

. where in respect of Data sourced directly from the Exchange, the Customer ceases to have satisfactory communications facilities in place in
accordance with clause 9, within 30 (thirty) days of receiving notice from the Exchange;

. it is required to do so by applicable law, is directed to do so by a competent regulator, or where such competent authority terminates its
authorisation to manage the relevant financial markets for which it redistributes the Data pursuant to the Agreement;
. the Service is generally terminated or suspended by the relevant Exchange;

. the Exchange reasonably believes that this is necessary to maintain the security or integrity of the Service or the Exchange’s operations or to
prevent their misuse; or
. for a reason beyond the Exchange’s reasonable control.

. Post-termination, the Customer may store and use the Data collected during the term of the Agreement only where such storage and use of
such Data is for compliance with applicable laws, regulatory obligations, or other such reasons approved in writing by the Exchange.

. Where the provision of the Service is suspended by the Exchange under clause 5.6.3, the relevant Exchange shall, at the request of Customer,
refund any pre-paid Charges on a pro-rata basis.

. Where the provision of the Service is terminated by the Customer under clause 5.2, the relevant Exchange shall, at the request of Customer,
refund any pre-paid Charges on a pro-rata basis.

. The Customer shall pay the applicable Charges for the Service as set out in the Price List and Data Product Schedule, and/or Market Data
Policy Schedule. Charges shall be payable within 30 (thirty) days of receipt of the Exchange’s invoice. Charges should be paid by bank transfer.

. All Charges are subject to Value Added Tax at the prescribed rate where applicable, and any other tax, duty or levy imposed by legislation. The
Customer shall be responsible for the timely payment of, or reimburse the Exchange on demand for, the full amount of all such taxes at the rate
applicable at the time. Where the laws of the Customer’s territory require the Exchange to make such deductions from a payment due to the
Exchange, then the amount due from the Customer to the Exchange shall be increased to an amount, which after making such tax deductions,
leaves an amount equal to the amount originally due to the Exchange.

. The Exchange may charge interest on overdue payments at the rate of the Bank of England base rate plus 8% per annum or the maximum
amount permitted by law (whichever is lower), accrued on a daily basis.

. Notwithstanding any other rights the Exchange may have under the Agreement, the Exchange shall have the right to suspend its Service in the
event that: (i) the Customer breaches clause 6.1 and such breach lasts for more than 30 (thirty) calendar days; and/or (ii) any submission of

information to the Exchange as specified in the Reporting and Audit Schedule is sent to the Exchange with more than 30 (thirty) calendar days
of delay.
. The Customer agrees (including on behalf of the Customer’s Subsidiaries) that:

. all Intellectual Property Rights and any other rights of whatever nature in and relating to the Service and the Data shall remain the property of
the relevant Exchange;
. it shall have no rights in or to the Data other than the right to use them in accordance with the express terms of the Agreement;

. the Exchanges have (or each has) made and will continue to make substantial investment in the obtaining, verification, selection, co-ordination,
development, presentation, and supply of the Data; and
. any goodwill generated through the Customer's use of the Trade Marks shall belong only to the relevant Exchange.

. Nothing in the Agreement shall transfer to the Customer any right or interest in any Intellectual Property Rights and the Customer shall have no
rights to use the same except as expressly set out in the Agreement.
. Each party represents and warrants that it shall perform its obligations in relation to the Agreement in compliance with applicable law.

. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Service and the Data is provided “as is” and on an “as available” basis. Neither Exchange makes any
warranties of any kind, whether express, implied, statutory, or otherwise, and each Exchange disclaims all implied warranties, including any
warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, good title, satisfactory quality and non-infringement. Neither Exchange shall be
liable to the Customer or any third party for any decisions based on the Data, for any inaccuracy, incompleteness, or error in the Data or in the
event that the Service is interrupted, changed or becomes unavailable for any reason. Neither Exchange warrants that the Service or the Data
will meet the Customer’s specific needs, achieve a particular result, be error free, complete or provided on a timely basis or not be susceptible
to intrusion, attack or computer virus infection.

. Subject to clauses 8.4 and 8.5, neither party shall be liable to the other, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty
or otherwise, for:
. any indirect, special, or consequential Loss;
. any Loss of profits, Loss of revenue, Loss of anticipated savings, Loss of goodwill, Loss of opportunity, or wasted expenditure;
. Loss of, damage to, or corruption of, data; or

. in the case of each Exchange, Loss or damage arising from any Claim made, or Loss incurred by, a client of the Customer, in each case,
regardless of whether such Loss is foreseen or foreseeable.

. Nothing in the Agreement excludes or limits a party’s liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent
misrepresentation, or any other liability that cannot be excluded or limited by law.

. The liability of each Exchange for its obligations under the Agreement shall be several and shall, subject to clause 8.4, extend only to any direct
Loss or damage arising out of its own total or partial failure to perform any obligation under the Agreement in respect of its Data. The Customer
agrees that it shall only bring a Claim against: (i) LSE in respect of any failures relating to LSE Data; and (ii) TGHL in respect of any failures
relating to TGHL or TGHE Data.

. Subject to clause 8.4, each Exchange’s liability for direct Loss or damage arising from its total or partial failure to perform any obligation under
the Agreement shall, in respect of any one incident or series of incidents attributable to the same cause, be limited in aggregate to:

. in respect of LSE, the total Charges paid by the Customer for the LSE Service in the 12 (twelve) months immediately preceding the date on
which the first event giving rise to the Claim occurred;

. in respect of TGHL, the total Charges paid by the Customer for the TGHL Service in the 12 (twelve) months immediately preceding the date
on which the first event giving rise to the Claim occurred.
. Nothing in the Agreement excludes or limits:

. the Exchange’s liability arising from:
8.7.2.1. the indemnity at clause 8.8.

. The relevant Exchange shall indemnify Customer and its directors, officers, employees and agents from third party Claims and Losses (other
than by a Group Company of Customer) to the extent the same arises out of or in connection with any allegation that the use by Customer of
any Data or Trade Marks licensed under the Agreement (other than any Trade Mark of a third-party information or services provider) infringes
such third party's Intellectual Property Rights. The foregoing shall be Customer’s sole remedy in respect of Claims and Losses to which this
indemnity applies.
. The relevant Exchange shall have no liability under the indemnity in clause 8.8 arising from or in relation to:

. the use of any Data or Trade Marks in combination with anything not provided by the relevant Exchange, or after the termination date of the
relevant Service;
. any content forming part of the Data that is not wholly owned or created solely by, or on behalf of, the relevant Exchange; or
. any error in data collection or storage by the Customer.
. The Customer shall indemnify each Exchange from third party Claims and Losses:

. to the extent the same arise out of, or in connection with, the use of the Service by the Customer or any third party because of the Customer;
or

. brought by the Customer’s Subsidiaries in respect of the Agreement, and any liability, costs, or expenses (including any reasonable legal costs
and any other reasonable expenses) included therewith.
. In relation to any Claim or Loss to which clauses 8.8 or 8.10 apply, the indemnified party shall:

. promptly notify the other party;

. not make any admission in relation to or settle, or attempt to settle, the Claim or Loss without the prior written consent of the indemnifying party
(not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed);

. allow the indemnifying party on request to have sole conduct of the Claim, provided that indemnifying party shall not settle, or attempt to settle,
the Claim without the prior written consent of the indemnified party (not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed);
. give the indemnifying party all assistance reasonably requested in dealing with the Claim or Loss; and
. subject to sub-clauses 8.11.1 – 8.11.4, take all reasonable steps to mitigate any Losses that are the subject of the indemnity.
. In relation to any Claim or Loss to which the indemnity in clause 8.8 relates, the Exchange may, in its sole discretion and at its expense:
. procure for Customer the right to continue to use any of the allegedly infringing Data licensed under the Agreement; and/or
. replace or modify any of such allegedly infringing Data to make it non-infringing.

sections.title: TECHNICAL COMPLIANCE AND CHANGES TO THE SERVICE

sections.text:
. Each Exchange reserves the right to determine the form and contents of the Service and, in particular, to modify and supplement from time to
time the technical, functional, administrative and operative methods of supply of the Service itself, wherever necessary for complying with
provisions of law or due to a change in the organisation of the financial markets or modifications or supplements to the Technical Specifications.
The relevant Exchange shall communicate to the Customer such modifications or supplements at least 30 (thirty) calendar days prior to their
entry into effect unless such modifications or supplements are a consequence of the compliance with provisions of law or due to an emergency
in which case no notice shall be provided to the Customer. In the event of modifications or supplements pursuant to this clause, the Customer
shall have the right to terminate the Agreement by providing 30 (thirty) calendar days’ written notice to the Exchange. The parties agree that
should such modifications or supplements prevent the Customer from receiving any Service for at least 14 (fourteen) consecutive calendar
days, then the variable component of the relevant Charges shall be reduced in proportion to the period in which the relevant Service has not
been utilised, it being understood that the Customer is obliged to communicate such impediments in a timely manner.

. The Customer undertakes that, in addition to the Agreement, it shall comply with applicable provisions contained in the Technical Specifications
(which the Customer acknowledges it has received or has access to on the Exchange’s website).

. The Customer acknowledges that the implementation of all operations necessary for the connection of its equipment (hardware and software)
with the Systems, as well as the maintenance of the above-mentioned equipment, shall not be the responsibility or cost of either Exchange.

. Neither Exchange shall have any obligations to provide the Service directly to the Customer under the Agreement unless the Customer has in
place satisfactory communication infrastructure to receive the Service, in accordance with such arrangements as may have been approved in
advance by the relevant Exchange in writing.
. Subject to clause 10.2, the parties shall keep confidential all Confidential Information.

. Either party may disclose Confidential Information to the following persons to the extent that such parties need to know the Confidential
Information for the purposes contemplated by the Agreement:
. its auditors, lawyers, or other professional advisers;
. its Group; and

. competent regulatory or governmental authorities to which either party is subject or reasonably submits, to the extent required by such
regulatory or governmental authority.

. The receiving party shall ensure that any recipients of the disclosing party’s Confidential Information are bound by confidentiality obligations
similar to those contained herein and shall be fully responsible for any breach of such confidentiality obligations by the recipient.
. Either Exchange may amend:
. these Terms and/or the Price List and Data Product Schedule at any time on 90 (ninety) calendar days’ written notice; or
. subject to clause 11.1.1, any Schedule that forms part of the Agreement on 30 (thirty) calendar days’ notice.
. any part of the Agreement where required for legal and/or regulatory reasons with as much notice as practicable.

. In the event the Customer considers any such amendment to be unfavourable, it may terminate the Agreement on the date the amendment
comes into effect, provided it gives the relevant Exchange at least 30 (thirty) days’ notice in writing, such termination to be effective on the date
the amendment in question is to come into effect.
. Except as provided in clause 11, the Agreement may only be amended in writing by duly authorised representatives of the parties.

. Subject to clause 12.2, any notice given under or in connection with the Agreement shall be in writing and shall be served by email to: (i) in the
case of each Exchange, marketdata@lseg.com or such other email address as either Exchange may notify the Customer in writing from time
to time; or (ii) in the case of the Customer, such email address as the Customer may notify the relevant Exchange from time to time. The deemed
effective date shall be the date of transmission.

. Any legal Claims or other documents related to any legal proceedings under the Agreement must be served in accordance with the laws or
rules applicable to such proceedings.

sections.title: ASSIGNMENT
sections.text: London Stock Exchange Market Data Terms and Conditions

. The Customer may not assign or transfer any rights or obligations under the Agreement without the relevant Exchange’s prior written consent,
such consent not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
Each Exchange shall have the right to assign any of its rights and/or obligations under the Agreement to another party, such assignment to
become effective on written notice to the Customer.

. No waiver on any breach of any provision of the Agreement shall constitute a waiver of any other breach, and no waiver shall be effective unless
made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of the waiving party.
. No failure or delay by any party in exercising any right or remedy under the Agreement shall constitute a waiver of that party's rights or remedies.

. The Agreement is the parties' entire understanding of the contract between them with respect to the subject matter and supersedes all prior
agreements, representations, and proposals, oral or written.
. Each party confirms that:

. in any event, without prejudice to any liability for fraudulent misrepresentation or fraudulent misstatement, neither party shall be under any
liability or shall have any remedy in respect of misrepresentation or untrue statement unless and to the extent that a Claim lies under the
Agreement; and

. in entering into the Agreement, it has not relied on any representation or warranty or undertaking which is not expressly set out in the
Agreement.

. If any provision of the Agreement is held by any competent authority to be invalid or unenforceable in whole or in part, the validity of all other
provisions (and, if applicable, the remainder of the provision in question) shall not be affected.

. All provisions of the Agreement that may reasonably be construed as surviving the termination of the Agreement shall survive such termination.
Without prejudice to the foregoing, the provisions of clauses 5.7, 5.8, 6, 7, 8.7, 10, 14, 15, 16 and 17 will survive the termination of the Agreement.

. Except as expressly provided otherwise, no term of the Agreement is enforceable under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 by a
person who is not a party to the Agreement.

. The Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in all respects in accordance with, the laws of England and Wales and subject to the
exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.

. Where there is a conflict between any of: i) these Terms; ii) any Schedules; and iii) an Order Form, the prevailing terms shall be those contained
in the following documents in prevailing order:
. the Order Form;
. where applicable, the Data Shop Schedule;
. these Terms;
. the Price List and Data Product Schedule;
. the Schedules other than the Price List and Data Product Schedule.
